title: Layers in a GIS

draft.title: Layers in a GIS
card: A geographical information system (GIS) is software that stores geographical data. It keeps each type of data as its own map layer.
Layers can show different things for the same area, such as soils, rainfall, rivers or roads. Each layer can be switched on or off.
Laying one layer over another lets you compare them. You can look for places where features match up or overlap, which may show a pattern.
A pattern shows that two things occur in the same places. It does not prove that one causes the other, so more evidence may be needed.
draft.remember: A GIS keeps each type of data as a layer, and overlaying layers helps you spot patterns.

a.q: A GIS has one layer for rivers and another for farms. What does laying the two layers over each other let you do?
opts: See whether farms tend to be close to rivers
Show that rivers are the cause of the farms
Combine rivers and farms into a single layer
Measure how much rain falls on each farm
a.why: Overlaying layers lets you compare where two things are, so you can see whether farms cluster near rivers. It does not prove rivers caused the farms, because a pattern only shows that things occur in the same places.
a.clue: Overlaying lets you compare where things are.

b.q: Tane uses a GIS in Tasmania. He overlays a layer of sheep farms on a layer of annual rainfall. Most farms sit in the areas with moderate rainfall. What can he conclude?
opts: There is a pattern linking sheep farms and rainfall
Rainfall alone has caused the farms to be there
Farms in Tasmania only exist in moderate rainfall
The rainfall layer has been changed by the farm layer
b.why: Overlaying the layers shows that the farms and moderate rainfall occur in the same places, which is a pattern. It does not prove rainfall alone caused the farms, because other layers such as soils or roads could also matter.
b.clue: A match in location shows a pattern, not a cause.

a.best: See whether farms tend to be close to rivers

b.best: There is a pattern linking sheep farms and rainfall
